paper.title: Fast Online Learning with Gaussian Prior-Driven Hierarchical Unimodal Thompson Sampling

settings.name_in_paper: n-armed stochastic bandit with Gaussian rewards
unmapped: System model allows arm-specific sigma_i, but the TSG posterior/analysis uses unit-variance Gaussian rewards N(mu_i,1)
settings.definition_quote: We study a system of $n$-arms ... in each round, the agent picks one arm and receives a stochastic reward $X_i(t)$ of arm $i$ that is drawn from a Gaussian distribution $X_{i}(t) \sim N(\mu_i,\sigma_i^2)$

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian bandit with clustered arms (strong dominance)
unmapped: Arms partitioned into known fixed clusters; learner knows the clustering
Strong dominance (Assumption 1): every arm in the optimal cluster beats every arm in any suboptimal cluster
settings.definition_quote: We study a system of $n$-arms that are clustered to $K$ subsets $\mathcal{K}=\{C_1,C_2,...,C_K\}$ ... Assumption 1 (Strong Dominance) For $C\neq C^*$, $d_C>0$.

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian bandit with clustered unimodal arms
unmapped: Arms partitioned into known fixed clusters
Mean reward unimodal over the known arm ordering within each cluster (Assumption 2); learner knows neighbor structure
settings.definition_quote: Assumption 2 (Unimodality in each cluster) For $\forall C\in\mathcal{K}$, the expect reward function among the cluster $C$ is a Unimodal function.

conditions: unit-variance Gaussian rewards as used by the TSG posterior

source.label: thm:1
source.quote: For an $n$-armed stochastic bandit problem, TSG has expected regret E[R(T)]\leq\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\frac{18\log(D_{max}T)}{\Delta_i}\right)+O(n). Where $D_{max}=\max_{i}\Delta_i^2$.

results.notes: Paper's n = number of arms (K canonical). Bound has explicit leading term 18 log(D_max T)/Delta_i plus O(n); recorded with O notation. Regret computed as sum Delta_i E[N_i], i.e. pseudo-regret. Noise variance assumption ambiguous (proof uses a parameter delta in place of sigma).

symbols.Delta_Cp: Delta'_C = min mean in optimal cluster minus max mean in cluster C

source.quote: Under Assumption 1, the expected number of plays of a sub-optimal cluster $C$ at time $T$ using TSCG is bounded by E[N_C(T)]\leq \frac{18\log(D_{max}T)}{\Delta_{C}'^2}+O(1).

results.notes: Bound on expected number of plays of a suboptimal cluster.

symbols.Delta_C: mu_star minus the smallest mean in cluster C
symbols.Delta_Cp: Delta'_C = min mean in optimal cluster minus max mean in cluster C
symbols.sum_opt_cluster: sum over suboptimal arms i in the optimal cluster C*

source.label: eq:proof8
source.quote: For an $n$-armed stochastic bandit problem under Assumption 1, the TSCG has an expected regret E[R(T)]\leq \sum_{C\neq C^*}\frac{18\log(D_{max}T)}{\Delta_{C}'^2}\Delta_{C}+o(\log(T))+ \sum_{i\in C^*}\frac{18\log(D_{max}T)}{\Delta_i}+O\left( n\right).

results.notes: o(log T) term dropped from expression (dominated). K here = paper's n (number of arms).

symbols.Delta_C: mu_star minus the smallest mean in cluster C
symbols.Delta_Cp: Delta'_C = min mean in optimal cluster minus max mean in cluster C
symbols.sum_neighbors: sum over neighbors of the optimal arm i* within its cluster

source.label: eq:proof29
source.quote: For an $n$-armed stochastic bandit problem under Assumptions 1 and 2, the UTSCG has an expected regret of E[R(T)]\leq\sum_{C\neq C^*}\frac{18\log(D_{max}T)}{\Delta_{C}'^2}\Delta_{C}+o(\log(T))+ \sum_{i\in Neighbor(i^*)}\frac{18\log(D_{max}T)}{\Delta_i}+O\left(n\right)+F. Where $F=\sum_{i\neq i^*}\left(\frac{12}{\Delta_i}+\frac{16\log(2\Delta_i)+4}{\Delta_i\sqrt{2\pi}}+2\sqrt{2\pi}\right)$

results.notes: F term expanded; o(log T) term dropped. K = paper's n.
